claim: The repository preserves a real failed acoustic epoch, a failed Uno resource observation, and a frozen V5 machine-native candidate with reproducible offline framing, checksum, identity, and evidence checks.
supported_conclusions: The first acoustic event model failed to discriminate quiet from intentional stimuli.
The raw piezo signal retained useful amplitude variation despite classifier failure.
The human-readable V4 interface did not fit the declared Uno program envelope.
V5 relocates human labels and telemetry formatting to the host while retaining readable external contracts.
The checked-in V5 framing and checksum decoder passes offline corruption and resynchronization tests.
unsupported_conclusions: V5 fits in Uno flash or SRAM.
V5 passes the preregistered physical reaction protocol.
The adaptive model is stable over long unattended operation.
The results generalize to other Uno boards, piezos, enclosures, or environments.
The study has earned formal MNCS or MNCDS conformance.
promotion_blockers: repository-bound arduino:avr:uno compile report for both V5 builds
complete preregistered V5 hardware stimulus run
protected stimulus custody and independent evaluator
long-duration stability and adversarial acoustic evaluation
electrical characterization of piezo input protection
